=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/persist_budget.py:328-350 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: In decide(), `start` resets only the max_hours clock after a governor escalation (`oldest = parse_ts(ordered[start]["ts"])`). `items = rounds(ordered, current_approach(ordered))` still counts every round in the history, so the `max_rounds`, `trailing_failed` and `no_progress` checks all see pre-escalation rounds.
  WHY: An issue escalated as `open_pr:max_rounds` and then resumed by a person escalates again after one more review round (`len(items)=6 >= 5`): ai:needs-human is re-added and "## Persistence budget reached" is posted again, which breaks the documented fresh-window promise. Severity disagreement: gemini says BLOCKER, the other three say MAJOR, so the highest is used. Suggested fix: compute `items` from `ordered[start:]` and add a resume-after-escalation table case.
- scripts/persist_budget.py:328-333 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The elapsed-time window starts after the latest governor escalation, but P6 (plan line 481) says to measure from the first journal entry.
  WHY: If a resumed issue's total journal history already exceeds PERSIST_MAX_HOURS, the decision can still be "continue", so the time cap no longer bounds total elapsed work. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5's notes accept the departure as documented and intentional.
- scripts/persist_postmerge_verify.py:605-767; scripts/persist_budget.py:316-317; scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:19675-19755 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: P5 hands a failed post-merge check to P6 whenever PERSIST_BUDGET_ENABLED is true, without checking that a trusted journal exists. P6 then logs `journal_absent` and makes no decision.
  WHY: With PERSIST_BUDGET_ENABLED=true and the default PERSIST_JOURNAL_ENABLED=false, P5 reopens the issue but suppresses its own /answer retrigger, so the intended re-plan never happens and nothing warns about it. Severity disagreement: gemini says BLOCKER, minimax and luna say MAJOR, so the highest is used. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 notes this is older code that the "Journal off" fragment bullet documents.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:persist_budget_govern_issue() | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: A standalone re-plan can make up to 4 writes (label edit, `/answer` comment, journal append, state comment), so 5 decisions per tick can total 20 writes.
  WHY: This contradicts the plan's "at most 2 writes per decision" constraint and raises the API rate-limit risk. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 notes an earlier round accepted the figure with documentation.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:30750-30764 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `PERSIST_BUDGET_STATE_CHANGED=true` is set whenever jq and mv exit 0, even when the jq select matches no wave issue and the file is byte-identical.
  WHY: The gate at ~31022 then calls `post_state_comment`, which PATCHes the state comment with unchanged content, adding up to 5 redundant writes per tick; a `cmp -s` guard is suggested. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 disputes reachability because the issue numbers come from the same state file.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "Stay inside the files the plan lists for P6." / "Implement only phase P6."
  expected_change_site: P6 `files_touched` grant on issue #8561 (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `docs/INVENTORY.md` are outside it)
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: The PR diff edits `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (ci.yml:672 adds `tests/test_persist_budget.py` to the pre-push gate step) and `docs/INVENTORY.md` (docs/INVENTORY.md:190 adds the `scripts/persist_budget.py` entry). Neither file is in the grant. Both edits are required by the CI guards (`tests/test_ci_wires_every_test_file.py`, `tests/inventory_parity.py`), and `tests/test_files_touched_scope_guard.py` flags them. The deviation is acknowledged and needs the grant widened or the test relaxed. Severity: gemini and glm say NIT, minimax says MAJOR.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/persist_budget.py:decide() | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The last run restarts the max_hours window after a governor escalation (`start = index + 1`; `oldest = parse_ts(ordered[start]["ts"])`), but `items = rounds(ordered, current_approach(ordered))` and the `if len(items) >= limits["max_rounds"] and MERGING_LABEL not in _labels(labels): trigger = "max_rounds"` check still count every round in the history. The governor entry is journalled with `--approach inherit`.
  WHY: An issue escalated as `open_pr:max_rounds` or `max_approaches:max_rounds`, once resumed, escalates again after one more review round (`len(items)` = 6 >= 5): ai:needs-human is re-added, another "## Persistence budget reached" comment is posted and another governor entry is journalled. Minimal fix: `rounds(ordered[start:], current_approach(ordered))` plus a table case "resumed after open_pr:max_rounds escalation, one new ok review round -> continue".
- NOTES (not findings, 6 related items): The max_hours restart (luna) departs from plan line 481 but is documented and needed. The P5 journal-off hand-off (luna) is older code, documented in the "Journal off" bullet. The state-changed nit (minimax) cannot fire because the jq select always matches. The IndexError at `ordered[start]` (gemini) is not reachable. Earlier rounds accepted the ci.yml/docs/INVENTORY.md scope edits, the "at most 2 writes" figure and the open-PR escalation order. Verified: `tg_notify_issue` signature (scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:766), the WARNING line is outside the alert-levels guard, the standalone flags are set on every pass of the loop (22859-22860), and the cached comments carry `user.login`.
- HARDENING: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh, standalone persist-budget hook, `_pb_standalone_comments=""` branch. When `_standalone_staged_support_cache_available` is "false", the hook passes an empty string even after branches 23028-23030, 22919 or 22973 already completed a paginated read, so the comments are read twice. Suggested fix: set a `_pb_comments_complete=true` flag and pass `comments_json` through unless it holds 100 or more comments (~4 lines). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/persist_budget.py:decide() function, specifically the use of `rounds(ordered, ...)` for round counting | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Rounds are counted across the full history of the current approach, even after a governor escalation (the "fresh window" promise).
  WHY: When a person resumes an issue escalated as `open_pr:max_rounds`, the next journalled round immediately returns `escalate` again, which strands the issue.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:Managed hook, persist_budget_govern_issue integration | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: P5 hands failed post-merge checks to P6 without checking that a trusted journal exists. P6 returns `journal_absent` and the poller skips the re-trigger.
  WHY: P6 does nothing for items handed off from P5, while P5 reopens the issue but suppresses its own replan.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:persist_budget_govern_issue() | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: A standalone re-plan can make up to 4 writes (label edit, `/answer` comment, journal append, stall-state comment), so 5 decisions per tick can total 20 writes.
  WHY: This contradicts the plan's "at most 2 writes per decision" constraint and raises API rate-limit risk.
- TASK_GAP | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  Requirement: "Stay inside the files the plan lists for P6." / "Implement only phase P6."
  Expected change site: The P6 `files_touched` grant (scripts/persist_budget.py, scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh, .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml, tests/test_persist_budget.py, tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py, tests/test_orchestrate_poll_workflow_contract.py, agents.d/8427-p6-persist-budget.md, changelog.d/8427-p6-persist-budget.md).
  Evidence of absence: The PR diff modifies .github/workflows/ci.yml and docs/INVENTORY.md, which are not in the grant. The edits are needed for CI parity but still deviate from the stated scope.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/persist_budget.py:decide(), lines ~328-344 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `start` slices `ordered` only for the max_hours window. `items = rounds(ordered, current_approach(ordered))` and the `len(items)`, `trailing_failed(items)` and `progressed(...)` checks still use the full list, so pre-escalation rounds are counted.
  WHY: After a person resumes an issue that hit `max_rounds=5`, the next round returns `escalate open_pr:max_rounds` again, re-adds `ai:needs-human` and re-posts "Persistence budget reached". The fresh-window promise is not applied consistently across the four triggers.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:around lines 30750-30764 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `PERSIST_BUDGET_STATE_CHANGED=true` is set whenever jq and mv succeed, even when the jq select matches no wave issue and the file is unchanged.
  WHY: The gate at line 31022 then calls `post_state_comment` with identical content, which can mean up to 5 redundant PATCH writes per tick. A `cmp -s` guard is suggested.
- scripts/persist_postmerge_verify.py:605-611, 734-767; persist_budget.py:316-317; orchestrate_poll_process.sh around line 19675-19755 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: P5 reopens failed-check-after-merge issues and defers its replan to the journal, and P6 reads the journal to decide. Neither checks that the journal is enabled, and `PERSIST_JOURNAL_ENABLED` defaults to `false`.
  WHY: With `PERSIST_BUDGET_ENABLED=true` and `PERSIST_JOURNAL_ENABLED=false`, the poller does real work but makes no governed actions and logs `journal_absent` without warning. A one-shot `journal_disabled` guard on each hook entry is suggested.
- TASK_GAP | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  Requirement: "Stay inside the files the plan lists for P6." (per linked issue scope, and per the `files_touched` grant in the orchestrator metadata)
  Expected change site: The P6 grant: `scripts/persist_budget.py`, `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`, `.github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml`, `tests/test_persist_budget.py`, `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py`, `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_workflow_contract.py`, `agents.d/8427-p6-persist-budget.md`, `changelog.d/8427-p6-persist-budget.md` (and the broad `tests/**`, `changelog.d/*`, `agents.d/*` globs).
  Evidence of absence: The PR also edits `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (pre-push affected-test gate step) and `docs/INVENTORY.md` (`scripts/persist_budget.py` entry), and neither is covered by the grant. CI guards (`tests/test_ci_wires_every_test_file.py`, `tests/inventory_parity.py`) require both edits, and `tests/test_files_touched_scope_guard.py` flags them. The grant on #8561 must be widened or the test relaxed before merge.
- TASK_GAP | severity=NONE | confidence=5
  Requirement: PR body uses `Refs` (never an auto-close keyword) for the orchestrator tracking issue.
  Expected change site: PR body composed by the pipeline.
  Evidence of absence: The body uses "Refs #8427" for the tracking issue and "Closes https://github.com/shubhodeep1/coding-workflows/issues/8561" for the sub-issue, which is correct per §21. This passes; no gap.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
